title: Your Evening and Sleep
description: Find out what really keeps you up late and wrecks your sleep pattern.

questions.es_1: I deliberately delay sleep to get free time for myself that I don't get during the day.
questions.es_2: As soon as my head hits the pillow, my brain starts going over the mistakes I made today.
questions.es_3: I always promise 'just one more video or episode', but end up going for hours.
questions.es_4: Because my daytime schedule is controlled by others (boss, lecturer, parents), night is my time to feel free.
questions.es_5: I often wake up in the middle of the night with my heart racing, thinking about tomorrow's work.
questions.es_6: I feel I need intense screen entertainment (competitive gaming or scrolling) right before closing my eyes.
questions.es_7: Going to bed early feels like ending the day's fun too soon.
questions.es_8: The quiet of the night brings negative thoughts I've been holding back to the surface.
questions.es_9: Even when I'm very sleepy, my fingers keep scrolling social media automatically.
questions.es_10: I'm annoyed with myself the next morning for staying up late, but I do it again that night.
questions.es_11: I often plan worst-case scenarios about my future while trying to fall asleep.
questions.es_12: I can't imagine falling asleep without a YouTube video or movie playing in the background.
questions.es_13: The busier and more draining my day, the more I push myself to stay up for entertainment at night.
questions.es_14: Watching the clock tick toward morning makes me more panicked and even less able to sleep.
questions.es_15: Boredom while getting ready for bed feels unbearable, so I reach for my phone as an escape.
questions.es_16: I feel sleep steals the precious leftover time I could use to relax.
questions.es_17: I've tried all kinds of breathing techniques for sleep, but my mind is too busy to relax.
questions.es_18: A notification arriving after I've closed my eyes immediately tempts me to open my phone again.
questions.es_19: I know staying up late harms my health, but the late-night freedom feels worth the risk.
questions.es_20: I tend to grind my teeth or clench my fists without realizing it while trying to sleep.
questions.es_21: The pull of late-night chatting or gaming with friends is much stronger than my sleepiness.
questions.es_22: To me, night is a sanctuary where no one can make demands of me.
questions.es_23: Before sleep, I replay the day's social interactions and feel embarrassed about what I said.
questions.es_24: After working hard all day, my brain demands a 'reward' (dopamine), and sleep doesn't feel like one.

results.description: You sacrifice sleep to win back the 'me-time' you lose to daytime busyness and demands.
Your body is tired, but your brain is noisy. Night is when overthinking and anxiety peak.
You stay up because you get pulled into entertainment (games, social media, series) that gives instant dopamine until you lose track of time.
